Article Title: Nepal floods revive Bihar’s annual nightmare: Why the state faces flooding every year
Article Text:
The rivers that sustain the region for most of the year turn dangerous during the monsoon

What was the trigger this time?

Why does Bihar drown every year?

Class I refers to flash floods, which occur due to rainfall in Nepal, have a short lead time of around eight hours between forecast and flood, and recede quickly.

Class II refers to river floods, with a lead time of 24 hours and floodwaters that take a week or more to recede.

Class III refers to drainage congestion at river confluences, where the lead time exceeds 24 hours and the water lasts the entire monsoon season, receding only after about three months.

Class IV refers to permanently waterlogged areas.

Embankments: Solution or part of the problem?

Everybody loves a good flood

The traditions around floods

NEW DELHI: Boats replacing cars on flooded roads, families moving to relief camps and swollen rivers spilling into villages. North Bihar is bracing for familiar scenes once again as floodwaters from Nepal move downstream.Floods have long been a part of life in northern Bihar. But a growing population and rapid urbanisation have made their impact more severe over the years.The rivers that sustain the region for most of the year turn dangerous during the monsoon. And for people living here, there is little choice but to face the floods, rebuild and prepare for the cycle to repeat itself.Bihar minister Ramkripal Yadav said the state government is closely monitoring the flood threat in Bihar in view of the tragedy in Nepal."Bihar is adjacent to Nepal, and the water that has come from Nepal in the past has affected many areas of Bihar, leading to loss of life and property, destruction of crops and homes. The Bihar government and the chief minister himself are monitoring this," Yadav told ANI.He assured that the state government will extend every possible help to those affected."The Bihar government will provide every possible help. The flood victims of Bihar have the first right on Bihar's treasury, and it is secure for them.The government will work," he added.A glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered a flash flood in Nepal that has claimed more than 600 lives.Analysis of satellite imagery indicated that a large mass of ice and rock may have fallen into the Lende Khola river, temporarily blocking its flow and creating a natural dam that later breached, sending floodwaters downstream.Due to the collapse, a large volume of ice and rock debris entered the Lende Khola, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi river in Nepal, generating a sudden surge that carried water, sediment and large boulders downstream.The scale of the devastation can be gauged from the fact that twelve hydropower plants were reportedly knocked offline, dozens of bridges were swept away and the only road connecting the valley to the rest of Nepal was destroyed.Nature could not care less about political borders. And a flood that originated in Nepal will not stop at the border. From Nepal, the floodwaters will eventually move into north Bihar, before flowing into West Bengal and eventually Bangladesh, where they will empty into the sea.Speaking to The Times of India, IIT-trained civil engineer and flood expert Dinesh Mishra said Bihar's locational disadvantage is one of the reasons why it drowns every year in floods. He said the state is situated in such a way that water comes directly through the south-flowing rivers from Nepal."The first reason is Bihar's locational disadvantage. Bihar is situated in such a way that water comes directly from the mountains," Mishra said."All the rivers that enter Bihar from Nepal are south-flowing. So, the area north of the Ganga will inevitably remain waterlogged. And if it does not, there will be drought in the region," he added.Rivers originating from the Himalayas, like Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak and Bagmati, carry huge volumes of silt with them to Bihar. When the water level increases due to rain, these rivers overflow their banks.This makes Bihar India's most flood-prone state, with 76 per cent of the population in north Bihar living under the threat of floods.Bihar's disaster management authority classifies floods into four categories.This year, according to Bihar water resources department, the Gandak river has crossed the danger mark in Gopalganj, while the barrage at Valmikinagar released around 99,800 cusecs of water at 8 pm on Saturday."The water level of several rivers, including the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and the Ganga, has been rising. Incessant rainfall in the catchment areas of Nepal has led to rivers touching or flowing above the danger level at several places," a senior official of the water resources department said.People in West Champaran, East Champaran, Sitamarhi and Muzaffarpur, besides Gopalganj, Saran and Vaishali, have also been facing heightened fears over the past three days following an unprecedented inflow of water from Nepal.Other than flooding, another concern is soil erosion along the banks of swollen rivers.For over a century, embankments along rivers have been a major preventive measure against floods. Successive governments built these walls along river banks to prevent rivers from deviating from their course and protect settlements.However, Dinesh Mishra said these embankments are the root cause of the havoc wreaked by floods rather than being the solution."You build embankments basically to prevent river water from spilling out. But if floodwater that would naturally flow into the river is stopped, the water has nowhere to go," Mishra said."If it cannot return to the river, it will move into areas that were previously not affected by floods," he added.Mishra said Kosi once had space to spread and deposit its sediments, but embankments have now confined the river. With the sediments having nowhere to go, the riverbed has been rising, making the Kosi increasingly prone to overflowing."The river carries silt with it, and because of the embankments, the riverbed continues to rise," he said.Interestingly, Flood Atlas of Bihar, prepared by Isro along with the central and state governments, also says that "there must be a realisation that minimising the risk and damage from floods may be a more rational way of flood management rather than formulating structural measures along the dynamic rivers such as the Kosi."During the conversation, Mishra, however, rejected the notion that floods have always been a source of sorrow for Bihar. He said floods are also a time of celebration.He said farmers eagerly wait for floods because, as he put it, "a fresh layer of silt is deposited on the fields after floods, making the soil more fertile."He added that in the remote villages of north Bihar, people sometimes wait for floods because relief funds and the attention of politicians are also drawn towards villages where little development work has been done."People have been made this way. Earlier, they had clear SOPs to protect themselves during floods. But now, because they have become dependent on the government for relief, lives are lost," he said.For generations, floods in north Bihar were not simply seen as a force to be feared. They were woven into the rhythm of life, with people learning to live alongside the rivers rather than trying to keep them at bay."Our ancestors knew this was a water-rich, flood-prone region. When they settled here, they must have done so with that understanding," Mishra said.The relationship with the rivers was deeply personal. People revered them as mothers, and when the rains failed, women in villages would perform rituals to invoke the rivers and call for water.But when the floodwaters refused to recede, another ritual would follow. Women would gather with fruits, flowers, sandalwood, akshat and sindoor to persuade the river to leave.The rivers were considered unmarried, Mishra said, and women would even "threaten" them with marriage if they refused to listen.These traditions show how closely floods have been tied to life in north Bihar for generations.People did not always see the rivers only as a threat. They depended on them for water, fertile soil and agriculture, even as they feared the destruction that came when the rivers overflowed.That relationship continues even today. Every monsoon, the same rivers bring both relief and anxiety. And once the water recedes, people clean their homes, return to their fields and begin rebuilding knowing that the floods may return the next year.
Article Summary: A glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered a flash flood in Nepal that has claimed more than 600 lives. Bihar minister Ramkripal Yadav said the state government is closely monitoring the flood threat in Bihar in view of the tragedy in Nepal.

Article Title: ‘No question of bringing back Article 370’: BJP hits out at Mirwaiz Umar Farooq
Article Text:
Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, chief cleric of Kashmir, was criticized by the BJP's Jammu and Kashmir unit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP Jammu and Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur on Sunday rejected Kashmir's chief cleric chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq 's call for political parties to unite for the restoration of Article 370 , saying there was "no question" of bringing back the constitutional provision.Thakur said Parliament had taken a "historic" constitutional decision to abrogate Article 370 and that the Supreme Court had subsequently upheld it. He accused the Mirwaiz of making statements that could disturb the peace that has returned to the Valley after years of violence."Mirwaiz Umar Farooq needs to realize that Article 370 will not be reinstated. No political party, leader, or pressure group can undo the fundamental truth that Parliament has permanently buried Article 370," Thakur said.He said attempts to revive the issue risked pushing Kashmir back into a period of political instability."These kinds of statements are intended to incite people and disturb the tranquility of the Valley once more. This will never be permitted. The return of peace to Kashmir has come at a very high cost to the country. Thakur stated, "We cannot allow politically motivated statements to undermine or challenge the sacrifices made by our courageous security forces and civilians, including political workers who gave their lives for peace and democracy.Thakur said people in Kashmir should not be pushed into another cycle of violence, shutdowns and unrest after having endured years of disruption."Those who try to resurrect old fault lines need to realize that Kashmir has progressed. Our young people are looking for the chances to educate themselves, work, entrepreneurship, investment, and travel. "They don't want to go back to a time, when violence dictated the future and shutdown calendars controlled their lives," he added in the statement.Thakur said political parties were free to express their views within the Constitution, but argued that repeatedly seeking reversal of a constitutional decision upheld by the Supreme Court was futile."Democracy gives the right to speak and participate, but democracy cannot be reduced to repeatedly demanding the reversal of a constitutional decision that has already been upheld by the highest court of the country," he stated.He also reiterated the BJP's position that statehood for Jammu and Kashmir would be restored at an appropriate time, while insisting that statehood and Article 370 were separate issues."Statehood and Article 370 are clearly different. The government has declared that statehood would be restored at a suitable moment. However, there is no way that Article 370 could be reinstated,". "Those who are causing confusion on this matter need are advised to stop misleading the public," he stated.Earlier, Mirwaiz had criticised the National Conference government's performance, saying its current position differed from commitments made during the 2024 Assembly elections."The people's rights have been taken away, Jammu & Kashmir has been split, and all of our legal and constitutional obligations have been totally disregarded," he said.While acknowledging that issues such as electricity, roads and development were important, Mirwaiz said they were secondary to what he described as the broader question concerning the status of Jammu and Kashmir.“ But I think these are secondary issues. The real issue is that the very existence of the people of Jammu & Kashmir is under threat. At this juncture, all political parties in J&K should not only raise their voice for the restoration of statehood but also seek the restoration of Article 370, which was the basis accession (with India),” he stated.Mirwaiz also alleged that the Union government had broken its commitments to the people of Jammu and Kashmir dating back to 1947, including constitutional guarantees.
Article Summary: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, chief cleric of Kashmir, criticized by the BJP's Jammu and Kashmir unit. Thakur said attempts to revive the issue risked pushing Kashmir back into a period of political instability. He accused the Mirwaiz of making statements that could disturb the peace that has returned to the Valley.

Article Title: NEET-PG 2026 exam at Jaipur centre rescheduled to September 5 over power outage
Article Text:
File photo: Students wait outside an examination centre before appearing in the NEET-PG 2026 examination

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The NEET-PG 2026 examination at a Jaipur centre has been rescheduled to September 5 after concerns over a power outage and technical disruptions during the test on Sunday, according to National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) sources.The examination at iON Digital Zone Sitapura 2 in Jaipur will be reconducted for all candidates allotted to the centre. Nearly 300 candidates were scheduled to appear for the examination there.NBEMS sources said further details regarding the rescheduled examination would be communicated separately to the affected candidates.The development came as candidates at two iON Digital Zone centres in Sitapura reported technical disruptions during the NEET-PG examination.According to news agency PTI, candidates alleged that the examination started late and computer systems repeatedly shut down after the test began.Some candidates claimed their systems went down six to seven times during the examination, while others alleged that the disruption occurred even more frequently. They said that after the systems restarted, only a few questions appeared on some computers before they went down again.Several candidates came out of the examination centre amid the disruption and staged a protest, questioning the technical arrangements.They also raised concerns about whether the technical failures could affect the fairness of the examination and demanded an impartial inquiry.A candidate, Gunjan, said aspirants paid a substantial fee for an important examination such as NEET-PG but were not provided adequate technical infrastructure for an uninterrupted test.Candidates said many aspirants had prepared for the examination for one to two years and feared that the disruptions could affect their future.Police and administration officials reached the centre following the protest. ACP Jaipur South Lalit Sharma said police were deployed at the spot to maintain law and order amid the commotion.Meanwhile, the NEET-PG 2026 examination commenced across the country on Sunday, with more than 2.73 lakh medical graduates appearing for the postgraduate medical entrance examination at designated centres.The examination was conducted by NBEMS in computer-based mode in a single shift from 9 am to 12:30 pm.NEET-PG is held for admission to postgraduate medical courses across the country.
Article Summary: NEET-PG 2026 examination at a Jaipur centre has been rescheduled to September 5. Concerns over a power outage and technical disruptions during the test on Sunday. Nearly 300 candidates were scheduled to appear for the examination there.

Article Title: ‘Frustrated’ Delhi man murders schizophrenic son, 2 held
Article Text:
Talukdar Ansari and his friend Mohammad Wasim alias Akram

Man, friend kill son with mental illness





NEW DELHI: A 64-year-old man and his friend have been arrested for allegedly killing the man’s 38-year-old son by assaulting him with a stone and strangling him in southeast Delhi’s Kalindi Kunj.Talukdar Ansari told police that his son, who was schizophrenic, had become aggressive and he was frustrated by his behaviour. Ansari also said he couldn’t arrange for his son’s treatment, investigators said.Ansari’s friend has been identified as Mohammad Wasim alias Akram (49). Both work as tailors. The deceased was Gul Hasan, said police.On Aug 23, police were informed around 7.13pm about the body of an unidentified man lying inside an abandoned container near the NTPC wall in Kalindi Kunj.The spot was around 500 metres east of Delhi-Mumbai Expressway.Police personnel who went to the site spotted an injury mark on the man’s head, while a concrete stone with apparent bloodstains was found nearby. murder case was registered and joint CP Vijay Kumar formed teams under the supervision of DCP Vineet Kumar.After several days of analysis of CCTV camera footage, investigators traced the movements of the victim, later identified as Hasan, and found him travelling with two men towards the crime scene.The two men were subsequently traced to a stitching factory in southeast Delhi’s Govindpuri. Ansari and Wasim were apprehended Friday afternoon by a team led by ACP Anil Sharma and comprising station house officer Raman Kumar and others.Ansari claimed that Hasan was suffering from mental health problems, which police described as schizophrenia. Ansari allegedly said Hasan had even attacked him and other family members.“He also told us that he was not able to get him proper treatment. So he, along with his friend, made the plan a few days ago,” police said.According to investigators, they took Hasan to the abandoned container on the pretext of taking him to a doctor.Once they reached the secluded location, Wasim allegedly struck him with a stone, following which Ansari also assaulted him. Hasan was then strangled with a rope made from cloth waste and the body was left there, police said.Inquiry revealed that they initially planned to push Hasan into the Yamuna , but abandoned it after finding people around when they reached the river.On the way to the isolated spot, Ansari bought samosas to keep Hasan engaged and unsuspecting.Police said they had recovered the concrete stone and the rope used in the murder and bloodstained clothes worn during the incident.
Article Summary: Talukdar Ansari told police that his son, who was schizophrenic, had become aggressive and he was frustrated by his behaviour. Ansari’s friend has been identified as Mohammad Wasim alias Akram (49). Both work as tailors, said police.

Article Title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke dares Maharashtra govt to file cases against him, says must fix schools
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said, Expired food items are being used to feed children in govt schools





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday challenged govt to file “not one but 100 cases” against him if exposing poor conditions in zilla parishad schools was a crime, insisting that FIRs would not stop his School Theek Karo (fix the schools) campaign.During visits to zilla parishad schools at Lohgaon and Karanjala in Hingoli taluka, Dipke inspected classrooms, benches, drinking water facilities and material used for preparing mid-day meals.Villagers and social activist Munir Pathan accompanied him and highlighted problems faced by students and staff.Dipke said he has been touring govt schools across Maharashtra to draw attention to inadequate infrastructure and other shortcomings.“Is it a crime to visit schools and point out the problems and lack of facilities there? If it is, file not one but 100 cases against me, but please ensure that the schools are improved,” he said.In a video shared on social media, Dipke alleged that expired spices were being used in mid-day meals served to students.“Expired food items are being used to feed children in govt schools. Would those sitting in power feed the same food to their own children? And if exposing this means FIRs against us, then please go ahead.We won’t stop exposing the truth,” he said.Dipke alleged that many govt schools lacked basic facilities, with insufficient benches and poorly maintained toilets.He also criticised the disparity between public and private education. “It is unfortunate that children of govt officials and elected representatives study in air-conditioned private schools while children from ordinary families are forced to study in classrooms in poor condition,” he said.Referring to ongoing tribal student protests, Dipke urged govt to address their concerns without delay.“Students are the future of the country. Govt should not ignore their issues any further,” he said.Dipke demanded that rural zilla parishad schools be provided infrastructure and amenities comparable to those available in private schools in cities such as Mumbai and Pune.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday challenged govt to file ‘not one but 100 cases’ against him if exposing poor conditions in zilla parishad schools was a crime. Dipke said he has been touring govt schools across Maharashtra to draw attention to inadequate infrastructure and other shortcomings.

Article Title: Punjabi influencer Manjeet Kaur, who died after being 'tied to a tree, burnt alive', was 7 weeks pregnant: Autopsy
Article Text:
Manjeet Kaur (Image Credit: Instagram)

CHANDIGARH: Social media influencer Manjeet Kaur, 28, was nearly seven weeks pregnant when she died in hospital after allegedly being abducted from Chandigarh and set on fire in Morinda, according to her autopsy report.Kaur died during treatment at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh on August 26, nearly two months after she suffered severe burn injuries.Also read: ‘Why was her statement not recorded': 6 mysterious questions in influencer's death Police are now trying to trace and arrest two suspects, identified in the FIR as Shubhi and Pinda. They have been booked for kidnapping and murder following a complaint by Kaur’s mother, Kanta Devi.According to the complaint, Shubhi and Pinda, who were acquaintances of Kaur, called her to Sector 34 in Chandigarh on the intervening night of July 3 and 4.They allegedly assaulted her, forced her into a vehicle and took her to a forested area near Morinda, where she was allegedly tied to a tree and set on fire.Another acquaintance who reached the spot later managed to put out the flames using a blanket, police said.Kaur was initially taken to a hospital in Morinda before being shifted to Max Hospital in Mohali. She was later admitted to PGIMER, where she remained under treatment until her death.Also read: Who was Manjeet Kaur? Inside the life of Punjabi influencer who died after being 'set on fire' The case has also raised questions over an alleged delay in recording Kaur’s statement.Sources said Kaur regained consciousness during her treatment and sought to have her statement recorded. The PGIMER police post reportedly informed Kharar Sadar police that she was conscious and in a condition to give a statement.The information was also conveyed to the investigating officer, but he allegedly did not reach the hospital, sources said.A daily diary report (DDR) was reportedly recorded at the PGIMER police post regarding the communication.After Kaur died on August 26, the PGIMER police post again informed Kharar Sadar police. The investigating officer subsequently reached the hospital.Kaur’s mother was later taken to the Sector 34 police station, where her statement was recorded and an FIR was registered on Wednesday night.Police are now investigating the circumstances surrounding Kaur’s alleged abduction and death, as well as the events leading up to the attack.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Manjeet Kaur, 28, was nearly seven weeks pregnant when she died in hospital. She died during treatment at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh on August 26. Police are now trying to trace and arrest two suspects, identified in the FIR as Shubhi and Pinda. They have been booked for kidnapping and murder.

Article Title: PM Modi received by Uzbek President Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, leaders share car ride
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi with Uzbekistan Shavkat President Mirziyoyev

PM Modi's 'car' diplomacy

Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a warm and personal welcome from Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev after arriving in capital Tashkent on Saturday for a two-day state visit.From the airport, the two leaders travelled together by car to the presidential palace, marking the latest instance of PM Modi sharing a car ride with a world leader. They held a dinner meeting at the presidential palace.During the visit, the first leg of the prime minister’s two-nation tour, PM Modi will hold delegation-level talks with the Uzbek president to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries.The discussions will cover cooperation in trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties, while also setting the agenda for future bilateral engagement.In his departure statement, PM Modi noted that the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership had witnessed “significant advancement” in recent years.“I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan,” he wrote on X.The visit marks his fourth trip to Uzbekistan since taking office.He previously visited the country in 2015, 2016 and 2022.From Tashkent, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, which will mark 25 years of the organisation.PM Modi first “carpooled” with a world leader during his 2014 visit to the United States, when he shared a car ride with then-US President Barack Obama.However, since last year, car rides with world leaders have become a recurring feature of what has been described as the prime minister's "informal diplomacy."In September last year, during his visit to China for the SCO Summit, PM Modi travelled in the same car as Vladimir Putin, reciprocating the gesture months later when the Russian president visited New Delhi in December.Since then, he has shared car rides with world leaders including French President Emmanuel Macron, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi arrived in capital Tashkent on Saturday for a two-day state visit. He will hold delegation-level talks with the Uzbek president to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries. The two leaders travelled together by car to the presidential palace, marking the latest instance of PM Modi sharing a car ride with a world leader.

Article Title: Mirwaiz backs NC MP, demand for J&K statehood, Article 370
Article Text:
Mirwaiz Umar Farooq backs NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi urges for the restoration of Article 370 and statehood to the union territory.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Saturday backed National Conference MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi and criticised the governing party for failing to honour its election promises.He urged all political parties in J&K to raise their voice for the restoration of Article 370 and statehood to the union territory.“I think it is not only Aga Ruhullah Sahib but all political parties, organisations should stand up for the rights of the people and constitutional guarantees,” Mirwaiz told reporters here.While Mirwaiz has consistently spoken about the “rights of the people of J&K,” this is perhaps the first time he has openly criticised the NC for abandoning its position on Article 370 and backed Mehdi, the Srinagar MP who has been vocal in demanding its restoration.Mirwaiz said priorities of the NC govt are different from what it promised to people during the 2024 assembly polls. “The rights of the people have been snatched away, Jammu & Kashmir has been divided, all our legal and constitutional commitments have been completely ignored,” he said.Mirwaiz said electricity, roads and development are important issues which the govt is concerned with. “But I think these are secondary issues.The real issue is that the very existence of the people of Jammu & Kashmir is under threat. At this juncture, all political parties in J&K should not only raise their voice for the restoration of statehood but also seek the restoration of Article 370, which was the basis accession (with India),” Mirwaiz said.He said all promises made to people of J&K from 1947 onwards by the union govt were subsequently reneged upon, including the constitutional guarantees.On Friday, Mehdi, who is also influential Shia cleric, announced he has decided to resign from both the NC and the Lok Sabha and will formally send his resignation letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker on Nov 3, the 26th death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, who was killed by terrorists in an IED blast.Mehdi was responding to the NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah’s statement that he should resign and contest elections on his own rather than criticising the party for giving up on Article 370.Mehdi also shot off a letter to Dr Abdullah. “I am repeatedly sermonized about the impracticality of my political position. But what is Article 370, if not shorthand for the struggle to restore the dignity, honour, constitutional guarantees and liberties of our people? Nearly 65% of Jammu & Kashmir’s population is young, and their future is increasingly uncertain, with no jobs and opportunities. Our land is up for grabs.Our resources benefit everybody but us. Our religious rights, traditions and language face constant pressure. Our environment is being ravaged by illegal deforestation, mining and construction in ecologically fragile zones,” the letter reads.
Article Summary: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq backs NC MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi urges for the restoration of Article 370 and statehood to the union territory. Mirwaiz said priorities of the NC govt are different from what it promised to people during the 2024 assembly polls. Mehdi announced he has decided to resign from both the NC and the Lok Sabha.

Article Title: Union ministers Chirag Paswan, Jitan Ram Manjhi clash over quotas, demand each other's resignation
Article Text:
Chirag counters HAM

How Manjhi responded

SC-ST quota row

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the creamy layer principle be applied to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)? Yes, it should be included. No, it is not necessary. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday and sought each other's resignation.The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of the quota policy, backing the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the reservation regime.“I think the purpose of reservation has not been served. The concept of creating the Mahadalit category with 18 of the 22 Dalit caste groups has been defeated due to the wide gap among the beneficiaries. The Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) category was created out of the other backward castes (OBCs), and the same was true for the concept of economically weaker sections (EWS) among the upper castes,” Suman had said.“How can it be wrong to ask which sections have benefited from reservation and to what extent, and which people standing at the very bottom of the social ladder remain deprived of it? Why is no DM or SP from the Musahar community, which has 4 percent population in Bihar? A comparative study is needed.Why will one section get 8 percent and another 80 percent among the beneficiaries?” he added.The remarks, however, did not sit well with another NDA ally, Chirag Paswan. The Union minister of food processing industries said that if Manjhi and his son want sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then the Union minister should resign."People ask, 'Why isn't there a 'creamy layer' provision?' Well, let them give it up, then - let them stop availing the benefits of reservation," Chirag said."If Jitan Ram Manjhi feels these measures should be implemented, should he not resign first? Let him introduce the 'creamy layer' concept - after all, he would fall under that category too, wouldn't he? He should resign, and his son - who is present here - should resign as well," he added.He also asserted that the basis of reservation lies in social factors and discussing it from an economic perspective "goes against the Constitution.""The basis is social - specifically, the issue of untouchability within society," he said.Later in the day, Jitan Ram Manjhi slammed his cabinet colleague, accusing him of not caring about poor people."People will end up being deprived of the benefits of reservation because of this stance. However, we maintain that this division is essential in the broader public interest."Since he (Chirag) does not want to look after the interests of our poor people, he should resign," he added.The controversy stems from a 2024 Supreme Court judgment that allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to ensure that the benefits of reservation reach the more backward groups within these categories.It also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation.The Centre, however, told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the creamy layer principle cannot be extended to SCs and STs. It said the principle currently applies only to Other Backward Classes (OBCs)."It has nowhere specifically been held that the principle of creamy layer is applicable to SCs and STs. The reference made to the concept of creamy layer… appears to be the general observation with regard to reservation in respect of OBCs (Other Backward Classes)/SEBCs (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)."
Article Summary: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday. The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitans Ram ManJhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of quota policy.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General M M Naravane on Saturday described Operation Sindoor as "very necessary action", stating that it marked a significant shift in India's approach towards Pakistan. Naravane said India moved beyond targeting terrorist bases along the border to striking their supporters and infrastructure deep inside Pakistan, signalling a more assertive response to cross-border terrorism.Speaking to reporters in Vadodara after attending an event, Naravane, the 28th Chief of the Army Staff, said India’s earlier responses to terror attacks, including the Uri and Pulwama attacks, had largely focused on terrorist hideouts close to the border.“Operation Sindoor, which took place after the Pahalgam attack, was a very necessary action... Previously, whenever such attacks occurred, like after Uri, and Balakot strikes after Pulwama -- we were mostly targeting terrorist hideouts close to the border,” he said, news agency PTI reported.“But this time, the strikes carried out targeted their supporters and those who provide them backing, wherever they may be -- not just near the Line of Control, but deep inside Pakistan, in Muridke and Bahawalpur, from where they receive this support,” he added.Naravane said the operation sent a message that those supporting terrorism could not escape Indian action regardless of where they were located.“As our defence minister Rajnath Singh had said, 'we will enter their territory and eliminate them', and there will be no protection for them. So, this was a very significant shift in our modus operandi,” he said.Asked about reports of increased Pakistani activity in the Sir Creek sector and the reported “Operation Ababil”, Naravane said such activities take place but he did not have complete information about the reported operation.“These kinds of activities keep happening. I don't have complete information about this right now since I am retired,” he said.“I would like to say that whatever activity takes place, our forces always keep a close watch on it. There is nothing to panic about, and whatever action needs to be taken, appropriate action will be taken at the right time,” he added.Asked whether Pakistan was capable of taking on India, Naravane replied, “In my opinion, no.”On India-China relations, Naravane said the recent meeting between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi should be viewed against the backdrop of the long-standing boundary dispute between the two countries.“This discussion that took place, the 25th round of Special Representative-level talks between Ajit Doval from our side and Foreign Minister Wang Yi from China, is not happening for the first time,” he said.Naravane said the lack of a clearly demarcated boundary, both on maps and on the ground, was the key issue behind periodic disputes between the two countries.“Exactly where the boundary lies has not been clearly demarcated either on maps or on the ground. It is because of this lack of demarcation that occasional disputes arise between India and China,” he said.On theatre commands, Naravane said the debate over reorganising the armed forces along integrated theatre lines had been underway since the Kargil War.“The discussion on theaterisation first began after the Kargil War. It has already been 25 to 26 years since then. Theaterisation is not a new concept; it is a continuous process and an evolution,” he said.“Considering the way the nature of modern warfare is transforming and decision cycles are becoming progressively shorter, it is essential that we move toward theaterisation as expeditiously as possible,” the former Army chief added.Operation Sindoor was a significant demonstration of India's military and strategic capabilities, combining military and non-military measures to neutralise terrorist threats and deter Pakistani aggression. The multi-dimensional operation reinforced India’s zero-tolerance approach to terrorism while maintaining strategic restraint and securing international support.
Article Summary: Former Army chief General M M Naravane described Operation Sindoor as "very necessary action" He said India moved beyond targeting terrorist bases along the border to striking their supporters and infrastructure deep inside Pakistan.Naravane said the operation sent a message that those supporting terrorism could not escape Indian action regardless of where they were located.

Article Title: Have you done the truth test?
Article Text:
Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in Kural 423:Epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum ApporulMeipporul kaanbadhu arivu.“Wisdom is to discover the truth in whatever is heard, irrespective of who says it.”Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement.Iago’s words were believed because of who he appeared to be. Valluvar asks us to reverse that instinct: not “Who said this?” but “Is this true?”Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Someone tells you that your closest friend has been speaking against you. At work, you hear that a colleague has spoiled your chances of a promotion. What do you do? Do you believe the person who told you, simply because you consider that person honest and dependable? Or do you pause and ask: How do I know if this is true?Shakespeare gave us a tragic answer to this question in ‘Othello’. Iago manipulates Othello by describing how his wife Desdemona’s handkerchief was with his friend Cassio, driving Othello into a jealous rage. The tragedy was not merely that Iago lied. It was that Othello failed to examine. He ended up killing Desdemona.How, then, does one ascertain truth? Is there a method by which we can distinguish what is real from what is merely reported, assumed or imagined?Interestingly, our ancestors believed in measuring everything accurately. Whether it was a piece of cloth or the jaggery needed for a pot of payasam, things had to be measured. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement. But measurement was not confined to physical objects. Indian philosophy also explored ways of measuring truth itself.These methods are called ‘pramanams’, means by which valid knowledge about what is true is obtained. Traditionally, six pramanams are described.The first is ‘pratyaksha’, or ‘kaatchi alavai’ — knowledge through direct perception using any of the senses. I smell gas and conclude there is a leak.The second is ‘anumana’, or ‘karuthal alavai’ — inference. I see smoke rising from a distance and infer that there must be a fire.The third is ‘agama pramanam’ or ‘urai alavai’ — knowledge obtained through texts.The fourth is ‘upamana pramanam’ or ‘uvamai alavai’ — knowledge through comparison. Understanding the unknown through knowledge about the known.The fifth is ‘arthapatti’ or ‘porul alavai’ — postulation from circumstances. The house is unusually quiet. We may infer that there was a big fight and now everybody is silent. It is not direct knowledge, but a conclusion drawn from circumstances.The sixth is ‘anupalabdhi’ or ‘inmai alavai’, knowledge through non-perception or absence. If someone claims to have seen a polar bear in Antarctica, the claim can be rejected because polar bears are native to the Arctic.These are not merely philosophical categories, but disciplines for the journey towards truth. Without them, our minds can easily become prisoners of assumptions and biases.Bias is perhaps our first obstacle. If someone we admire says something, we are inclined to accept it. If someone we dislike says the same thing, we may instinctively reject it. In both cases, we judge the statement by the person rather than examining its truth.The pramanas provide a framework to go beyond what our eyes can see without letting imagination outrun reason. They help us test assumptions, examine evidence and separate fact from illusion.
Article Summary: Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement.

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.

CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response (File photo)

Judge must get fair chance to respond: CJI Surya Kant

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response. Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26. CJI Kant: “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media’

Article Title: No intention to quit politics, Nitin Gadkari clarifies
Article Text:
Statement taken out of context, not political: Gadkari’s office.

Statement taken out of context, not political: Gadkari’s office

NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari ’s office said on Tuesday that his remark that the younger generation should be given more responsibility as “he could no longer take on as much work as before”, had been misinterpreted to suggest that he intended to quit politics.In a statement clearly prompted by speculation triggered by the minister’s comment on Sunday, his office emphasised that Gadkari’s remarks were “specifically about the Laxmanrao Mankar Trust”, an organisation established by him that runs Ekal Vidyalayas in tribal areas.Nitin Gadkari’s office said, “In that context, Gadkari said that he could no longer take on as much work as before and that the younger generation should be given an opportunity to take greater responsibility. His remarks were clearly related to the functioning and future leadership of the Trust. However, some television channels are presenting the statement as a political remark, taking it out of its actual context. ”At an event in Nagpur on Sunday, Nitin Gadkari had said that he has been in active public life for over three decades and during his political journey, he has experienced many ups and downs, fulfilled various responsibilities, and received many honours.
Article Summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari ’s office said on Tuesday that his remark that the younger generation should be given more responsibility had been misinterpreted to suggest that he intended to quit politics. His office emphasised that his remarks were “specifically about the Laxmanrao Mankar Trust’.

Article Title: Is the viral video really Kai Cenat being assaulted by police? Here’s the truth
Article Text:
Getty Images

Viral Kai Cenat police assault video was misidentified

Why the false Kai Cenat claim spread so quickly

A video claiming to show streamer Kai Cenat being assaulted by a police officer has gone viral across social media, sparking outrage among viewers who believed the popular creator was involved. However, the footage has been misidentified. The man seen in the video is not Cenat, and the incident actually occurred during a traffic stop in Blytheville, Arkansas. The real confrontation involved a passenger and a state trooper, while Cenat had no connection to the incident.The footage circulating online does show a genuine confrontation between a police officer and a man, but claims identifying the person as Kai Cenat are false. According to the report, the incident occurred earlier this month in Blytheville, Arkansas, after a trooper stopped a vehicle that had allegedly been traveling at a dangerous speed.The situation reportedly escalated when a passenger resisted the officer's commands. The trooper then broke the vehicle's rear window and physically removed the passenger from the car. The man subsequently faced charges related to obstruction and resisting.While the use of force shown in the footage has prompted discussion online, the key issue surrounding the viral post is the identity of the person involved. It was not Kai Cenat.The confusion appears to have been fueled by the man's resemblance to Cenat. Once social media accounts attached the streamer's name to the clip, the claim quickly spread, with users sharing the footage alongside captions suggesting that Cenat had been confronted by police.Cenat is a hugely recognizable figure online, making the false identification particularly easy to spread. The streamer has also had previous encounters with law enforcement, including his 2023 arrest following the chaotic Union Square giveaway in New York, which may have made the new claim appear believable to some viewers.The incident highlights how quickly misleading captions can transform real footage into a completely different story. A dramatic police confrontation already has the potential to attract attention, but attaching the name of a major streamer like Cenat can dramatically increase its reach.According to the report, the false claim gained momentum after users connected the footage to Cenat without checking its original source or comparing the identities of the people involved. The result was widespread outrage over an incident the streamer was never part of.The episode also demonstrates the risks of sharing viral clips without verifying their context. Even when the underlying footage is authentic, the description attached to it can be completely false.Ultimately, the police encounter shown in the video is real, but the claim that Kai Cenat was the person assaulted or arrested is not. The footage originated from a traffic stop in Arkansas and involved another individual. As the clip continues circulating, viewers should be cautious about accepting viral captions as fact before checking where and when the original footage was recorded.
Article Summary: A video claiming to show streamer Kai Cenat being assaulted by a police officer has gone viral across social media. However, the footage has been misidentified. The man seen in the video is not Cen at, and the incident actually occurred during a traffic stop in Blytheville, Arkansas. The real confrontation involved a passenger and a state trooper.

Article Title: Nepal fights time, terrain to save 500 feared trapped in six hydro projects
Article Text:
Nepal's rescue agencies are battling rough weather and terrain to reach over 500 people trapped inside six hydropower projects in flood-hit areas.

TOI

TOI

TOI

DEHRADUN: Rescue agencies in Nepal are battling rough weather and terrain to reach more than 500 people believed to be trapped inside at least six hydro-power projects in the flash flood-hit areas, including the one in Rasuwa district, Nepal’s armed police toldon Saturday.The operations at the hydro-power plants are being carried out by the Nepalese army along with Nepal Armed Police Force (NAPF). While the army has deployed around 7,000 troops in the affected areas, NAPF has pressed nearly 4,000 personnel into service.Speaking with, NAPF spokesperson, deputy inspector general Netra Bahadur Karki, said: “The agencies’ focus is on the six projects which are upper Trishuli, upper Trishuli-1, Rasuwa hydropower, Trishuli 3A, Chilime Khola and Langtang hydropower projects. The exact number of people trapped inside is yet to be ascertained, but it is believed that at least 500 are stuck.”The joint teams are working continuously with available resources such as drones to rescue them, Karki said, adding the inclement weather along with road connectivity issues were making their task more difficult.“Due to rains, we’d to halt the operation in the morning and resume in the afternoon. Also, the road has been cleared for traffic for four wheelers upto Dhunche in Rasuwa district.Beyond that, only helicopters remain the mode of transport,” the officer said.Adding to the challenges, there are huge boulders and massive slush near hydropower sites, making it difficult to clear exit points to reach out to those trapped, said Karki. “The current rescue operations are one of the most challenging ones the force has ever taken up... 13 of our personnel have been missing since the first day of the tragedy.”A six-year-old girl trapped in slush under a damaged house in Rasuwa’s Timure area was rescued miraculously on Friday evening, Karki further said, adding that “the child remained under the debris for almost 60 hours before NAPF personnel spotted her due to her whimpers. She was identified as Manisha while her parents are yet to be found.”Meanwhile, Nepal’s army spokesperson, Brig Gen Rajaram Basnet toldSaturday: “Personnel involved in the rescue operations have to change their modus operandi frequently due to unfavourable weather conditions. Our personnel at Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel are using drilling machines to locate the tunnel’s exit point amid massive amounts of mud, slush, boulders deposited by the floods...”According to the officer, till 2.30pm on Saturday, the army men had airlifted 208 more people, including 38 Chinese and five Indian nationals, from Rasuwa to safer places.
Article Summary: Rescue agencies battling rough weather and terrain to reach over 500 people trapped inside six hydropower projects in flood-hit areas. Operations at the hydro-power plants are being carried out by the Nepalese army along with Nepal Armed Police Force (NAPF)

Article Title: Tipu Sultan cutout video with Pakistan reference sparks row in Karnataka, 23-year-old arrested
Article Text:
This video featured a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song referencing Pakistan





CHIKKAMAGALURU: Chikkamagaluru Police arrested a 23-year-old man on Tuesday for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid”, prompting heightened security in the district, police said.Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama clarified that the action was not related to the installation of the Tipu Sultan cutout itself.He said a similar cutout had been installed at Tipunagara at the same location, around the same time and with the same dimensions in previous years.According to Dayama, police had earlier told organisers they could continue with arrangements followed over the past five to 10 years, but would not permit any new cutouts or decorations.The issue surfaced around 5pm to 5.30pm when the cutout was used as the backdrop in a video and a song containing a word referring to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid” was added, the SP said.The video was later circulated through multiple social media accounts and came to the police’s attention, ANI reported.Police registered an FIR under Sections 196 and 299 and traced the account that first circulated the video, following which the 23-year-old local resident of Tipunagara was arrested and is being produced before a magistrate, Dayama said.He allegedly shared the video as his WhatsApp status, sent direct messages to some Instagram accounts and other individuals, and uploaded a reel on his Instagram account, police said.Police are also probing the role of others who may have viewed, shared or recirculated the content."We are still in the process of ascertaining their role. If someone else also with intention did the same, then we will definitely arrest them and produce them," Dayama said.The SP said police were also trying to identify the person who originally created the video. A request has been sent to Meta for the relevant IP address as part of efforts to trace the original account.Dayama said the situation in Chikkamagaluru remained peaceful and police had spoken to community leaders. He said action would be taken against anyone attempting to create disturbances.Police social media monitoring teams at both the district and police station levels were also closely monitoring the situation, he said.More than 300 Home Guards, four Karnataka State Reserve Police (KSRP) platoons and local police personnel have been deployed for security, Dayama said. The forces will continue to monitor the situation during the function and the upcoming procession."Everything is peaceful, everything is calm, and this function will go on," Dayama said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Chikkamagaluru Police arrest a 23-year-old man for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout. The video featured a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid’ The action was not related to the installation of the cutout itself.

Article Title: Hair stylist killed as MUV rams scooter at Bengaluru signal
Article Text:
Victim identified as 33-year-old-hair stylist, Naveen





BENGALURU: A 33-year-old hairstylist died on the spot after a rashly driven car rammed into his two-wheeler on Kaggadasapura Main Road on Monday.CCTV footage of the accident showed the MUV driver ramming into victim Naveen’s gearless scooter, which was stopped at the Vijnananagar signal, throwing him into the air and killing him instantly.Police arrested the accused driver, identified as 63-year-old K Ramanan, a retired techie.Ramanan told police that he lost control of the vehicle out of anxiety and caused the accident.
Article Summary: A 33-year-old hairstylist died on the spot after a rashly driven car rammed into his two-wheeler on Kaggadasapura Main Road on Monday. Police arrested the accused driver, identified as 63- year-old K Ramanan, a retired techie.

Article Title: Ghaziabad robbery: 2 held after gunfight, Rs 5 lakh of looted Rs 25 lakh recovered
Article Text:
Ghaziabad police apprehended two individuals following a gunfight on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway





GHAZIABAD: Ghaziabad police arrested two people for allegedly robbing Rs 25 lakh from a Meerut-based businessman on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway under the jurisdiction of Wave City police station.The arrests were made after a gunfight in which both accused received bullet wounds in their legs.According to police, the accused were identified as Saddam (20), a resident of Arthala, Sahibabad of Ghaziabad and Aasif (38), a resident of Meerut.A businessman carrying Rs 25 lakh in a bag was stopped right in the middle of Delhi-Meerut Expressway by armed men who blocked his Thar with two cars, held a pistol to his head and fled with the cashThe robbery took place around 7pm on Friday, when traffic continued to pass around the vehicle, oblivious to the crime the gang carried out inside the Thar.Gillaman, a Meerut businessman who owns a factory recycling waste material, was driving to Jafrabad in Delhi with his cousin Samad and relative Saleem to pay for supplies. He left Meerut around 5pm and reached Dasna in a couple of hours, when he was stopped on the expressway.Police registered an FIR against unknown persons under the section of 309 (4) (robbery) of BNS in Wave City police station.Priyashri Pal, ACP of Wave City said that on Tuesday early hours, the SWAT team and Crime Branch received information from an informer that the accused wanted in Case of a robbery of Rs 25 lakhs with Meerut based businessman on Delhi-Meerut Expressway, were roaming in the area on a Splendor motorcycle.On the information, the SWAT team, Crime Branch, SWAT team Nagar Zone, and Police Station Wave City police team started checking in the Wave City area.“During checking, 02 persons riding on one Splendor motorcycle without number plate were seen coming. When the police team tried to stop them, both motorcycle-borne persons, seeing the police checking and being surrounded by the police team, turned the motorcycle around and started fleeing back. When the police team chased them, they abandoned the motorcycle and started firing at the police team with the intention to kill. In retaliatory action, in the police encounter, both fleeing persons were injured after being shot in the leg and fell down. They were immediately sent to the hospital for treatment and their condition is stable,” she said.From the possession of the accused, the looted Rs 05 lakh was recovered along with 02 illegal country-made pistols of 0.315 bore, 04 live cartridges, 04 empty cartridges and a Splendor motorcycle without number plate were recovered.
Article Summary: A businessman carrying Rs 25 lakh in a bag was stopped right in the middle of Delhi-Meerut Expressway by armed men who blocked his Thar with two cars. The robbery took place around 7pm on Friday, when traffic continued to pass around the vehicle, oblivious to the crime.

Article Title: CM Suvendu Adhikari orders probe into Jadavpur University ‘anti-national’ graffiti
Article Text:
‘Anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus; CM Suvendu Adhikari





KOLKATA: CM Suvendu Adhikari on Monday ordered a probe into ‘anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus, telling the VC and the principal secretary of the higher education dept: “If the presence of such anti-national messaging and deranged psychotic drawings is verified, immediate steps must be taken to remove the graffiti, fix accountability and initiate strict administrative and legal action against those responsible. ”Posting the videos on his X handle, the CM said his office “has received concerning videos and photographic representations through the CM’s Grievance Cell from conscientious students of Jadavpur University, reporting instances of objectionable, sociopathic, violent and anti-national wall graffiti and drawings inside the Arts Division Boys Hostel premises,” adding, “Under no circumstances will campus premises be permitted to be used as platforms for spreading deranged propaganda and anti-India sentiment. ”The CM stated, “The Bengal govt strictly follows zero tolerance policy towards anti-national activities anywhere in the state, especially on campuses. The concerned dept and university administration must ensure stringent compliance and the preservation of academic integrity.”He added, “West Bengal’s educational institutions must remain centres of merit and discipline, not grounds for divisive rhetoric and unsocial activities.”
Article Summary: CM Suvendu Adhikari ordered a probe into ‘anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus. He told the VC and the principal secretary of the higher education dept: “If the presence of such anti-national messaging and deranged psychotic drawings is verified, immediate steps must be taken”

Article Title: Ladakh protests: Sonam Wangchuk leads Leh candle march, seeks inquiry report into 2025 violence
Article Text:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk led a candle march in Leh to remember last year's violent clashes





LEH: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Monday led a candle march in Leh as part of a month-long programme to remember those who died in the violent clashes in Ladakh last year, while demanding the release of the inquiry commission’s report into the September 2025 violence this month.Wangchuk said August 24 to September 24 would be observed to commemorate the events of September 24, 2025, when protests over statehood and inclusion of Ladakh in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution turned violent.A BJP office was set on fire during the unrest and at least four people were killed in police action that followed.Speaking on Monday, Wangchuk said the inquiry commission’s report should be released this month, arguing that the delay was affecting public confidence. He also said a “decisive meeting” between the Leh Apex Body (LAB), Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and the Centre was expected in the first week of September to discuss Ladakh’s demands."This entire month, from August 24 to September 24, is being observed to honour and remember the events of 24 September 2025, which was a dark day. It was a day when five of our young men were martyred, and many others were injured, left disabled, or critically wounded.We began with a small candle march; it was kept small because His Holiness the Dalai Lama is currently in Ladakh. Once he departs, we will commemorate this month with much greater intensity," Wangchuk said.Recalling last year’s protests, he said Ladakh had been seeking its demands for six years and that a hunger strike began on September 10 after delays in addressing them."Regarding the situation over the past year: Ladakh has been demanding its rights for six years, but faced with delays and reluctance, people began a hunger strike on September 10 to make their voices heard peacefully. By the 15th day, when participants had to be hospitalised in critical condition, the public became deeply distressed and angry; circumstances arose, or were perhaps engineered, that led to some violence, and there is a pressing need for an investigation into this. "Wangchuk demanded that the report of the inquiry commission, headed by a retired judge, be made public, ANI reported."We are also calling for action regarding the Inquiry Commission led by a retired judge; a full year has passed, yet no decision has been reached. This delay is eroding public confidence. We hope that the Inquiry Commission's report will be released this month. Regarding the decisions concerning Ladakh's demands, discussed on May 22, no subsequent meeting has taken place to date. We hope that a decisive meeting will take place in the first week of September, as promised; otherwise, we will have to make our voices heard much more loudly, albeit peacefully," Wangchuk said.Wangchuk, who had spearheaded the protests along with the LAB and KDA, was detained for 170 days in Jodhpur Jail following the violence and was released in March 2026.The LAB and KDA have been demanding inclusion of Ladakh in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. The Centre, meanwhile, has proposed that the Union Territory administration constitute an Autonomous Hill Development Council in each of Ladakh’s seven districts under a framework based on Article 371.Ladakh’s administrative map expanded from two districts to seven in April, when Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass were notified.The next round of talks with the Union Home Ministry is expected in September.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk led a candle march in Leh as part of a month-long programme to remember those who died in the violent clashes in Ladakh last year. Wangchuk said August 24 to September 24 would be observed to commemorate the events of September 24, 2025, when protests over statehood and inclusion of Ladakh in the Constitution turned violent.

Article Title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah
Article Text:
Rahul addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress

In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes. He also cited a childhood anecdote of how then PM Indira Gandhi did not take seriously the US administration’s attempt to flatter her via the then First Lady.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said ‘we’ will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.
